name: This Man
title: Eight Thousand People Dreamed Him. Then Someone Drew Him.
claims: This Man is described as a conceptual art project and hoax created by Italian sociologist and marketer Andrea Natella | 1
The "Ever Dream This Man?" website said the first image was sketched in January 2006 by a well-known psychiatrist in New York based on a patient's description | 1
A second patient recognized the drawing days later; four more people recognized it after it was sent to colleagues | 1
The site claimed more than 8,000 people in cities worldwide recognized the man, including Los Angeles, Berlin, Tehran, Lagos, Tokyo, Moscow | 1
Dream accounts varied: romantic or sexual fantasies, attacks and crime against the dreamer, cryptic life advice | 1
In one account he was the dreamer's father; in another a schoolteacher from Brazil with six fingers on his right hand | 1
He rarely spoke; sounds are harder to remember in dreams than images; a recurring message was "go North" | 1
Flyer text: "EVER DREAM THIS MAN? Every night, all over the world, hundreds of people see this face in their dreams..." with www.thisman.org | 1
Story gained attention in 2008-9; views skyrocketed in October 2009 with more than two million visits and 10,000-plus emails | 1
On October 12, 2009 a comedian tweeted that it was scaring him | 1
People suggested he resembled fictional characters from Twin Peaks and The Twilight Zone, and public figures such as Andrew Lloyd Webber and Stephen Hawking | 1
An Indian guru claimed to be This Man as proof of his miraculous powers | 1
An actual living human who looked like This Man was never identified | 1

ThisMan.org posited five theories: Archetype (Jung), Religious (manifestation of God), Dream Surfer (outside force, supernatural or corporate mental conditioning), Dream Imitation, Daytime Recognition | 1
A 2014 Mysterious Universe article cited Jung and Ervin László's pseudoscientific Akashic Field theory and asked whether people could access the same information in dreams | 1
Users on forums like 4chan and blogs like io9 grew suspicious in late 2009 | 1
A WHOIS lookup showed the host owned guerrigliamarketing.it, a fake advertising agency founded by Natella that designed subversive hoaxes and weird art projects | 1
In 2015 Natella told Vice he first dreamt of This Man in winter 2008 and that the man invited him to create a website | 1
The identikit image was created with the mobile app Ultimate Flash Face | 1
In 2010 Natella posted on the site of KOOK Artgency, confirming he invented the story as a publicity stunt | 1
Natella said the original sketch was based on a photo of a real person from his own life when young (kept non-identifying) | 1
Natella said he was inspired by dream invasion in movies and books and wanted to explore the internet's power to spread urban legends and collective myths | 1
He elaborated in a 2012 paper titled "Viral 'K' Marketing" | 1
Natella never confirmed a commercial purpose; The Kernel said it was "almost certain" it was a guerrilla campaign for a film project by Bryan Bertino and Ghost House Pictures | 1
In May 2010 it was announced Bertino used the story for a screenplay titled This Man, produced by Ghost House Pictures; press release quote about an ordinary guy | 1
Ghost House claimed it bought the site, but the domain had not changed hands by 2013; no further news, option expired, Italian producers did not pick it up | 1
Serious coverage continued into the mid-2010s; in 2015 Vice interviewed Natella, who answered as if legitimate, and Vice published a retraction hours later admitting it fell for the hoax | 1
Vice's retraction said it could be verified as fake with a single google and that sometimes they mess up | 1
io9's Annalee Newitz called it Natella's greatest masterwork, citing it as uncanny, cheesy and a little bit scary and not pseudo-intellectual politics | 1
Vice described the hoax's purpose as priming people to dream what they've never dreamed, like Inception with memes | 1
Memes replaced the face with figures such as Karl Marx and Barack Obama; Comedy Central made a parody flyer | 1
A 2020 Spanish-Italian film Heste Hombre and a 2024 Japanese film This Man were based on the story; manga, a Dylan Dog comic and a K-pop music video referenced it | 1
Dream Scenario (2023), starring Nicolas Cage, centres on an unexceptional man appearing in thousands of people's dreams, and its premise is described as inspired by the "This Man" publicity stunt | 2
